posts.body_html:
I Just found out from Bristol that flickr has been bought out by smugmug: www.theguardian.com/technology/2018/apr/23/flickr-bought-by-smugmug-yahoo-breakup so we might experience a "photobucket situation" where possibly billions of photos will disappear from the internet pretty soon. To us, this means probably 10's of 1000's of photos on this forum, so enjoy as many posts as you can for the time being! If we're lucky, they won't bust a hostage situation and the pics of the past will be preserved, but it's hard to say what will happen.

For all you tech savvy nerds out there, any suggestions to free photo hosting websites where we can upload lots of photos to post on this forum? I liked flickr because they didn't alter the quality of the image. It seems photo hosting these days is lot like investing: place your photos on several different hosting sites so they don't all disappear if one site decides to change their policies.

posts.body_html:
May 2, 2018 22:38:16 GMT -5 gotsarrs said:
Their pricing isn't too bad. Not as good as free, but $40-$60 a year I can live with if I have to.


For sure, paying $40-$60/year just to keep the bulk of the existing photos on this site is way more than worth it. However, moving forward, if you have multiple websites that give you a service for free versus a site that has a fee for virtually the same service, you can guess where people will go.

I'm just thinking long term: say smugmug realizes in the short run or long run that their fee schedule for flickr isn't sustainable and they photobucket it to $400/year, that's my concern. Anytime you put all your eggs in one basket, you face this dilemma.

I think one way to keep photos on this site long term is to upload them to multiple different sites. One goes down, or one changes their policy, you still have pics here. Second strategy is to see if we can upload photos directly to the forum, and of course, if it costs money, we have member-donated auctions every year to pay for it. I can personally assure everyone those auctions will have great plants!

Jonny-than (the founder of the Sarracenia forum) is pretty nerded out, he might have other ideas since his computer nerdiness runs pretty deep, I'll shoot him an email shortly.

posts.body_html:
I use AWS S3 and haven't paid a dime yet (my traffic is too low, which also shows I shouldn't be paying a monthly or yearly fee to host), not at all worried about getting extorted later like what happened with Photobucket and will happen with any other free hosting service like that. It is not as intuitive as a standard photo hosting site, and it takes a little longer to post links, but the stability/security/functionality is worth it to me.

aws.amazon.com/s3/

aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/

I'm traveling now but can give more details when I return.
